capabilities: Grade submissions (notes, .txt, .pdf or pasted text) against a rubric note with a local Ollama model
Write draft grading notes with proposed scores, verbatim evidence quotes and draft student comments
Rebuild a grade book with per-criterion averages, score distribution and most-missed criteria
Check rubric notes for missing points, duplicate criteria and overlaps
Parse rubrics from markdown tables or bullet/heading outlines
disambiguation: Not a general teaching or course-management tool; it only grades submissions against rubric notes and rebuilds a grade book.
extras: Free and MIT-licensed; default model qwen3.5:9b needs about a 12 GB GPU and larger models grade more consistently. The README candidly warns that a 9B model misreads, over-rewards confident prose and sometimes invents quotes, and that dropped quotes and clamped scores are shown so users can judge reliability. Every score stays a proposal until the user types their own; no accounts, API keys or telemetry.
motivation: Institutions typically allow AI in grading only if no cloud model ever sees student names or words, so grading must happen locally.
problem: Instructors grading with rubrics have no AI-assisted grading in Obsidian that keeps student work entirely on their own machine, as institutions require.

relations.evidence: graded by a local model through Ollama

summary: Rubric-based grading assistant that grades student submissions with a local Ollama model, producing draft scores, verbatim evidence, comments and a grade book.
